lines.text: The Town Council at Weichfeld governs with a modest edge in its favour; where it asks it is generally given, and the exceptions are few enough that the clerks can name them.
The Town Council's standing at Weichfeld rests on the town's prosperity, which makes it exactly as durable as the prosperity is and no more.
What is settled at Weichfeld is the hall and only the hall; the town's steadiness is a statement about who answers, and not about what the answers will be.
Nobody at Weichfeld needs the trouble explained to them; it is recent enough that the town simply refers to it and moves on.
The Town Council at Weichfeld holds because Town Council is still the heavier of the two, and the weighing is done again every season.

lines.text: The town is behind whoever sits at Weichfeld, and a ruler with the town behind them can do things a ruler without it cannot attempt.
The town's business goes to a body rather than a person, and everybody has learned how long a body takes.

lines.pool: governing body name: a SLOT, never a baked noun
lines.text: What governs Weichfeld calls itself the Town Council, and the name is precise about the town's size and pretensions in a way outsiders routinely mistake.
The hall at Weichfeld is not organized into sides. The factions sit as factions, and nothing binds any two of them into anything larger.
The Guild Council's standing at Neubrücke is good and is doing work. The margin is what lets it spend goodwill on the decisions the town would otherwise refuse it.
Neubrücke credits the Guild Council with the good years whether or not the Guild Council earned them; the prosperity is the whole of the argument in its favour.
What is settled at Neubrücke is the hall and only the hall; the town's steadiness is a statement about who answers, and not about what the answers will be.
Nobody at Neubrücke needs the trouble explained to them; it is recent enough that the town simply refers to it and moves on.
A stranger at Neubrücke is told there is money in the town that does not come from the market, and is told no more than that.
Guild Council outweighs everyone who wants the Guild Council at Neubrücke, and the wanting is on the record. The hold is real and it is not comfortable.

lines.pool: legitimacyHold: public backing hardens the hold
lines.text: Public backing at Neubrücke is hardening the Guild Council's grip; what would be a contest elsewhere is an inconvenience here.
Nothing at Neubrücke governs cleanly. The Guild Council is an arrangement between kinds of power, and it decides at the pace of whichever of them is least willing.

lines.pool: governing body name: a SLOT, never a baked noun
lines.text: A stranger who addresses the Guild Council at Neubrücke by any other title is corrected, politely and immediately.
A stranger at Neubrücke cannot work out who is aligned with whom, and the reason is that nobody is.
The Guild Council's standing at Schwarzhain is good and is doing work. The margin is what lets it spend goodwill on the decisions the town would otherwise refuse it.
Schwarzhain credits the Guild Council with the good years whether or not the Guild Council earned them; the prosperity is the whole of the argument in its favour.
A stranger doing business at Schwarzhain needs one name and gets one answer, and can plan a season ahead on the strength of it.
Nobody at Schwarzhain needs the trouble explained to them; it is recent enough that the town simply refers to it and moves on.
There is somebody at Schwarzhain who does well out of arrangements the town does not enquire into, and the doing-well is the only visible part.
The Guild Council at Schwarzhain holds because Guild Council is still the heavier of the two, and the weighing is done again every season.

lines.pool: legitimacyHold: public backing hardens the hold
lines.text: There are people at Schwarzhain who would move on the Guild Council and do not, because moving on a ruler the town is behind costs more than the seat is worth.
What holds the Guild Council at Schwarzhain together is that no part of it can rule alone, and that is a stable arrangement exactly until one part can.

lines.pool: governing body name: a SLOT, never a baked noun
lines.text: The town at Schwarzhain calls the hall by its proper title in public and something shorter everywhere else, and both usages are precise.
A stranger at Schwarzhain cannot work out who is aligned with whom, and the reason is that nobody is.
